context.text: Stephanie Bice's Republican primary was canceled and she advanced unopposed.

candidates.name: Stephanie Bice
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced after the Republican primary was canceled

positions.summary: Her official issues page says she is a gun owner and will oppose efforts in Congress to limit Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: I will oppose radical efforts in Congress that would limit this important right.

positions.summary: In June 2026 supported the reconciliation bill that fully funds CBP and ICE through the end of the Trump administration.
positions.quote: Today’s legislation ensures that those who protect our southern border can not be held hostage again.

positions.summary: Her office states she has supported the SAVE Act in committee and on the floor, and describes her STEADFAST Act as in line with the SAVE Act.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Bice serves on the House Administration Committee and has supported voter ID and the Save Act both in committee and on the House floor.

record.text: Her Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Mineral Spacing Act (H.R. 1555), addressing duplicative federal permitting requirements for oil and natural gas development on lands where the federal government holds minority ownership, passed out of the House Natural Resources Committee.

Introduced the No Preference Act with Rep. Steve Womack (R-AR), which would bar the executive branch from giving federal contracting preference based solely on whether a contractor's workers are unionized.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. Record items drawn from her official House press releases.

candidates.name: Jena Nelson

priorities.text: Protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, and restore cuts to Affordable Care Act subsidies.
priorities.quote: Protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid. These programs are lifelines for vulnerable Americans—we must protect and strengthen them.

priorities.text: Cut the cost of living for working families through stronger antitrust enforcement and penalties for food and fuel price manipulation.
priorities.quote: Congress must cut the cost of living. While everyday working families struggle, the billionaires are getting richer.

priorities.text: Opposes cuts to veterans' healthcare, including reductions to VA hospitals and mental health crisis services.
priorities.quote: Trump wants to slash Veterans’ medical care by gutting the VA system. This would result in fewer hospitals, longer wait time and lower standards of care.

positions.summary: Supports restoring cuts to Affordable Care Act subsidies and expanding Medicare's power to negotiate prescription drug prices.
positions.quote: I will fight to restore the cuts to Affordable Care Act subsidies, and expand Medicare’s power to negotiate prescription medication prices

positions.summary: Supports windfall profit taxes and stronger antitrust enforcement to crack down on corporate price manipulation.
positions.quote: We need to crack down on corporate greed with stronger antitrust enforcement, windfall profit taxes, and penalties for food and fuel price manipulation.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page lists raising the minimum wage to $17 per hour among her proposals.
positions.quote: Raise the minimum wage to $17/hour, expand the Child Tax Credit and slash healthcare costs by letting Medicare negotiate drug prices.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; positions and biography are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and profile, so her career details are self-reported.

candidates.name: Robert Henri

priorities.text: Proposes 18 government reforms through Project Due Course intended to restore transparency and accountability in Washington.
priorities.quote: I'm proposing 18 government reforms through Project Due Course that will restore trust in our government, force transparency from the people in power, and demand accountability when laws are broken.

priorities.text: Argues Congress is unresponsive to popular demands and says more working-class representation is needed in office.
priorities.quote: Only about 2% of Congress comes from a working-class background, and that helps explain why so many Americans feel ignored by the people supposed to represent them.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site (projectduecourse.org) and Ballotpedia survey were reviewed; they cover government-accountability reforms (stock-trading ban, term limits, Supreme Court ethics, Pentagon audit), none of which map to the guide issues, so no positions or statements were added. His campaign website at ProjectDueCourse.org was reviewed and gives no education or employment history; no positions map cleanly to the guide's fixed issue keys, so none are listed.
